launched.sort: from the earliest launched to the most recent
launched.era: Drop each social network into the decade it launched.

rows.label: Instagram
rows.description: photo and video sharing social network owned by Meta Platforms
rows.hook: became the app where people share filtered photos and stories with friends and followers

rows.label: Facebook
rows.description: American online social media and social networking service
rows.hook: connected friends and family worldwide and became the first social network with over a billion users

rows.label: X
rows.description: American social networking service founded in 2006
rows.hook: let users post short public messages known as tweets to share news and opinions

rows.label: TikTok
rows.description: video-focused social media platform
rows.hook: made short, algorithm-driven videos a global phenomenon among young audiences

rows.label: Reddit
rows.description: American social news aggregation website and discussion portal
rows.hook: became known as the front page of the internet, home to countless topic-based discussion communities

rows.label: LinkedIn
rows.description: American social networking website for people in professional occupations
rows.hook: became the place professionals go to network, list resumes, and search for jobs

rows.label: GitHub
rows.description: hosting service for software projects using Git
rows.hook: became the place where millions of programmers host and collaborate on code together

rows.label: Pinterest
rows.description: American photo sharing and publishing website
rows.hook: became the go-to place for collecting ideas and inspiration on boards for DIY, recipes, and style

rows.label: Myspace
rows.description: American social networking website
rows.hook: was once the most visited social network before losing its dominance to newer rivals

rows.label: Tumblr
rows.description: microblogging platform and social networking website
rows.hook: became known for its freewheeling blogs and vibrant fandom communities

rows.label: Bluesky
rows.description: American social networking service
rows.hook: grew as an invite-only alternative built around user-controlled feeds and a decentralized network

rows.label: SoundCloud
rows.description: German business providing an online audio distribution platform
rows.hook: became the place independent musicians upload tracks and build a following directly, no label needed

rows.label: Google+
rows.description: defunct social networking service
rows.hook: was a short-lived rival social network built by a major search company that eventually shut down

rows.label: Xiaohongshu
rows.description: Chinese social media and e-commerce platform
rows.hook: became a hit in China for lifestyle reviews, shopping tips, and beauty trends

rows.label: Threads
rows.description: social networking site operated by Meta Platforms
rows.hook: was built by the makers of a hugely popular photo-sharing app as a text-based rival

rows.label: Tinder
rows.description: social network and dating platform
rows.hook: popularized swiping right or left to match with potential dates nearby

rows.label: WeChat
rows.description: messaging, social media, and payment app developed by Tencent
rows.hook: combined messaging, payments, and mini-apps into one super-app used daily across China

rows.label: VK
rows.description: social networking service from Russia
rows.hook: became Russia's largest and most widely used social network

rows.label: Letterboxd
rows.description: social network service for films
rows.hook: became the go-to app for film lovers to log, rate, and review every movie they watch

rows.label: ResearchGate
rows.description: commercial scientific social network
rows.hook: became a hub where scientists share papers and connect with fellow academics

rows.label: Tencent QQ
rows.description: instant messaging software service
rows.hook: was one of the earliest instant messaging platforms to dominate home computers across China
